about: Strict taxonomy of UI parts. Read taxonomy/SCHEMA.md. Checked by scripts/check-taxonomy.mjs.

features.definition: Draws a scene with depth and a camera (WebGL or similar), whether it decorates a section or carries content.
Exists to animate content that would be complete without it, or is a moving decorative backdrop with no information.
Concerns what the words say (voice, labels, punctuation, language), not how the text is set.
Defines named values that other parts read: color roles, light and dark sets, the brand slot, radius and shadow scales.
A small symbolic image standing for an action, object, person or organization: an icon, logo, wordmark or avatar.
Concerns how text is set: typeface, scale, weight, line height, tracking, line breaking, numerals, heading lockups or prose columns.
Lives inside a conversation with an AI assistant or agent: a message, composer, tool call line, agent status or agent question.
Shows goods for sale with a price or moves them toward purchase: product tile, option picker, cart line, order summary or checkout step.
Presents subscription or service plans with their prices, or estimates what a plan will cost.
Its content is a set of questions, each paired with its answer.
Shows evidence from third parties: words attributed to a named person, customer or partner logos, or certification marks.
Gives keyboard-first access to commands or places: a palette opened by a shortcut, hotkey bindings or the sheet that lists them.
A full-width horizontal band of a page that can be moved as one unit and usually carries its own heading.
The first band of the page, the one a visitor sees before scrolling.
Its whole job is to ask for one next step, with at most one alternative.
Sits at the very end of every page of a site or app, below all content.
Lists the top-level destinations of the whole site or app, or shows where the current screen sits among them.
Laid out as a vertical column docked to the left or right edge of the screen.
Positions things on a map of real places.
Its content is a set of items or steps placed in time order or in a fixed sequence.
Its only job is to say that something is loading or running, and optionally how far along it is.
Turns measured numbers into marks or figures meant to be read and compared.
Stands in for content that is not there: nothing yet, no results, a failure or missing permission.
Lets a person enter, pick or toggle a value that the product stores, submits or applies as a filter.

Drawn on a layer above the page that the person opens through a trigger (click, hover, focus or shortcut), or that blocks the page until it is dismissed; a toast that appears on its own and blocks nothing does not count.
Changes which panel, page or section of the same content is shown in place, without leaving the screen.
A control that runs one action or follows one link when pressed.
A message about something that happened or a condition that needs attention.
A short non-interactive tag naming a status, type or attribute of something else.
Records in rows that share one set of columns with headers.
The image, video or audio is itself the thing being looked at, alone or in a collection to browse; a thumbnail that stands for an article or a product does not count.
A bounded container for one item or one group of related content, or a list that repeats such containers.
Decides where regions sit and how they are separated: page frame, grid, section order, spacing, dividers or section surfaces.

classify.why: Depth and a camera need their own runtime and budget, whatever the scene is for.
An effect is judged apart from the content it moves, so it is classified before that content.
Wording rules hold for every part, so they are classified before any part kind.
Values read by every part come before the parts that read them.
A mark keeps one set of rules wherever it is placed.
Type setting holds for every part, so it is classified before any part kind.
A conversation has its own content model, so its parts go to it before any generic kind.
Goods with prices have their own content model, so they go to it before any generic kind.
Plans and prices decide the layout, whatever control shows them.
Questions with answers stay together, whatever control discloses them.
Third party evidence is judged for honesty first, whatever shape it takes.
Keyboard command access is a layer of its own, before generic overlays.
The opening band is judged as a whole, whatever it contains.
The end band repeats on every page, before generic navigation.
Global navigation docked to a side edge.
Any other global navigation is a bar at a screen edge or the trail under it.
A band whose whole job is one request.
A map is chosen by the data having places, before any generic chart.
Sequence outranks waiting and value encoding; a how-it-works band stays a section.
A pure waiting signal, before value encoding, because a progress bar is not a measurement.
Measured values drawn as marks or figures, including a band of figures on a page.
Every remaining page band explains the product or the organization.
A stand-in for missing content.
A control that keeps a value, before overlays, so a date picker with a popover stays an input.
A layer the person opens and dismisses.
In-place switching that keeps no value.
A single action control.
A message about an event or a condition.
A short tag that is not a control.
Rows that share columns.
Media as the content itself.
A container for one item, or a list of them.
Structure that places and separates regions.
Keeps the function total; a fixture that reaches this step fails the check, so it never decides a real part.

families.name: Page sections
families.definition: Full-width bands that make up a marketing or editorial page, each answering one question for a visitor.
includes: Bands that can be reordered on a page as one unit
The opening band and the closing request
Bands for plans, proof and common questions

excludes.what: Bars and rails that repeat on every page for moving around
The page frame, grid and spacing between bands
Charts and figures, even inside a band

examples: the opening band of a landing page
a band of plan cards
a closing band with one button

families.name: Navigation
families.definition: Parts whose job is moving a person between places of a site or app, or between views of the same content.
includes: Global bars and rails that list destinations
The end band with secondary links
Keyboard access to commands and places

excludes.what: Controls that run an action instead of moving
Menus and panels opened on a layer above the page

examples: a top bar with page links
a vertical app menu
tabs above a panel

families.name: Foundations
families.definition: The shared materials every other part is built from: page frame, item containers, type, wording, marks and theme values.
includes: How text is set and what it says

excludes.what: Effects that animate content that is complete without them
Parts with one job such as asking for an action or showing data

examples: a spacing scale
a type scale
a token theme with light and dark sets

families.name: Actions and inputs
families.definition: Controls a person presses to act, or uses to enter and pick values.
includes: Fields, selects, toggles, pickers and the forms that group them

excludes.what: Controls that switch views or move between places
Menus that open on a layer above the page

examples: a primary button
an email field with a label

families.name: Feedback and overlays
families.definition: Parts that report state, waiting, absence or events, and the layers a person opens above the page.
includes: Dialogs, drawers, popovers, tooltips and menus
examples: a status label
a saved toast
a confirm dialog

families.name: Data display
families.definition: Parts that present measured values, records, sequences in time and places.

excludes.what: Loading indicators, even when they show a percentage
A grid that places cards on a page

examples: a line chart of weekly revenue
a sortable table
a dated change log

families.name: Media, commerce and AI
families.definition: Parts whose content model belongs to one domain: media to look at, goods to buy, or a conversation with an assistant.
includes: Message threads, tool calls and agent status

excludes.what: A generic card for one item

examples: a thumbnail strip
a cart with an order summary
an agent reply with sources

families.name: Motion and effects
families.definition: Effects that add movement or depth to content that is complete without them, and three-dimensional scenes.
includes: Scroll reveals, marquees, number roll-ups and text effects
examples: a fade-up on first entry
a 3D globe behind a headline

categories.name: Hero
categories.definition: The first section of a page, which says what the page offers and gives the first action.
includes: The band a visitor sees before scrolling
Headline, one supporting sentence and the first action
A real product screen, photo or input placed in that band

excludes.what: A closing band that asks for the action again
A three-dimensional scene drawn behind the headline
Heading and eyebrow type rules shared across sections

examples: a headline beside a real product screenshot
a full-bleed photo with a short headline
an address field inside the opening band

categories.name: Feature and content section
categories.definition: A body section of a page that explains what the product or organization does, how it works or who it serves.
includes: How-it-works steps shown as a page band
Showcases that swap one frame between product screens

excludes.what: Ordered steps inside an app flow

examples: cards that each open with a measured result
a three step how-it-works band
tabs that swap product screenshots in one frame

categories.name: Pricing
categories.definition: Parts that present subscription or service plans with their prices so a person can choose one.
includes: Plan cards with aligned price and feature slots
Billing period switches for the plans

excludes.what: Prices of goods that go into a cart
Tables of records that are not plans

examples: three plan cards with a yearly toggle
a feature by plan comparison grid
a usage slider that shows the monthly cost

categories.name: Call to action
categories.definition: A section whose whole job is to ask for one next step, with at most one alternative.
includes: Closing bands with one sentence and one primary action
Entry splits that send each audience to its own path

excludes.what: The opening band of the page

examples: a closing band with one button
two entry cards for buyers and sellers
a last line that links to contact

categories.name: Testimonial, quote and proof
categories.definition: Evidence from third parties: quoted words attributed to a person, and marks of who uses or certifies the product.
includes: Customer quotes with name and role
Customer, partner and integration logo strips

excludes.what: The looping motion of a logo marquee

examples: a quote card that leads with a measured result
a single row of customer logos in one color
a pull quote with a large opening mark

categories.name: FAQ
categories.definition: A set of questions people ask, each paired with its answer.
includes: A title column beside a question list

excludes.what: An accordion of content that is not questions
An assistant answering inside a conversation

examples: questions separated by hairlines with one open answer
a title on the left and questions on the right

categories.name: Navigation header
categories.definition: A bar at the top or bottom edge of the screen that lists global destinations, together with the location trail under it.
includes: Site headers with links and one action
App top bars with title and page actions
Mega menu panels that list global destinations from the header

excludes.what: A vertical menu docked to a side edge
The band at the end of every page
Tabs that switch views inside one screen
A dropdown of actions opened from the bar

examples: a transparent header that turns solid on scroll
an app top bar with a sidebar toggle
a bottom tab bar with four destinations
a breadcrumb trail above a page title

categories.name: Footer
categories.definition: The band at the very end of every page that holds secondary links, legal text and contact.

excludes.what: A closing band that asks for an action above the footer

examples: brand and link columns with a legal row
one thin row with copyright and policy links

categories.name: Sidebar
categories.definition: A vertical column docked to a screen edge that lists the global destinations of an app.
includes: The drawer form of the same menu on phones
Workspace switchers at the top of the menu

excludes.what: A side panel with the details of one item
The frame that places the menu beside the content
A table of contents for one document

examples: a grouped app menu with a collapsed icon rail
a workspace switcher above menu groups

categories.name: Command palette and shortcuts
categories.definition: Keyboard-first access to commands and places: a palette opened by a shortcut, the hotkey bindings, and the sheet that lists them.

excludes.what: A search field that filters a list on the page
A dialog opened by a button

examples: a palette opened with a shortcut that filters commands and pages
a sheet listing keyboard shortcuts by area

categories.name: Tabs, segmented control and disclosure
categories.definition: A control that changes which panel, page or section of the same content is shown in place, without leaving the screen.
includes: Accordions and disclosure toggles outside question lists

excludes.what: A control that stores, submits or filters by a value
Global destinations of the site or app

examples: three underline tabs above a settings panel
a two option switch between list and grid view
page numbers below a list
a collapsible details row

categories.name: Layout and shell
categories.definition: The structure that decides where regions sit and how they are separated: page frame, grid, section order, spacing, dividers and section surfaces.
includes: App shells that place a sidebar, top bar and content
Layout rules that keep text readable at every width
examples: a figure row above chart panels on a dashboard
a form column beside a calm image on a sign in page
a print-like sheet layout for a report

categories.name: Card and list
categories.definition: A bounded container that presents one item or one group of related content, and the lists that repeat such containers.
includes: List rows with leading media and a trailing action
Tiles whose image stands for one article or result

excludes.what: Option cards that select a value
Rows that share one set of column headers
Collections of images or video to browse
The grid that places many cards
A product tile with a price

examples: a panel with a one pixel border and a tone step
a single-line row with a title and a trailing action
an article tile with an image and a thin caption

categories.name: Typography
categories.definition: How text is set: typefaces, scale, weight, line height, tracking, line breaking, numerals and heading lockups.
includes: Heading and eyebrow lockups for sections
Korean type setup and line breaking
examples: a fixed scale of title, subtitle and body sizes
a reading column with a comfortable measure
a section title with a small sentence-case eyebrow

categories.name: Copy and voice
categories.definition: What the words on a screen say: voice, labels, punctuation and language, independent of how they are set.
includes: Empty value traces that leak into text

excludes.what: Icons that stand in for words

examples: a button label that names the result
a headline built on one concrete fact
commas or colons used instead of long dashes

categories.name: Icon and mark
categories.definition: Small symbolic images that stand for an action, object, person or organization: icons, logos, wordmarks and avatars.
includes: Logos and wordmarks as supplied files

excludes.what: Photos and illustrations that are content
A row of customer logos shown as proof
Status dots that label a state

examples: a line icon beside a menu label
a round avatar that falls back to initials
the supplied logo file in the header

categories.name: Theme and tokens
categories.definition: The named values every part reads: color roles, light and dark sets, the brand slot, radius and shadow scales.
includes: Raw, role and component token layers

excludes.what: The switch a person uses to change the theme

examples: one brand variable on top of neutral roles
light and dark defined as token sets
a radius scale derived from one base value

categories.name: Button
categories.definition: A control that runs one action or follows one link when pressed.
includes: Icon-only buttons with an accessible name
Button groups that share one border

excludes.what: A control that keeps a value

examples: a solid primary button in the accent token
an outline secondary button
an icon-only close button

categories.name: Form and input
categories.definition: Controls that let a person enter, pick or toggle a value the product keeps, submits or filters by, and the forms that group them.
includes: Option cards that act as radio choices
Sign in, sign up and contact forms

excludes.what: View switches that keep no value
The submit action on its own

examples: a labeled email field with an inline error
a searchable select with grouped options
a row of filter chips above a list
a date field that opens a calendar

categories.name: Badge and label
categories.definition: A short non-interactive tag that names a status, type or attribute of something else.
includes: Counts on a tab or a menu item
Data honesty labels such as measured or estimated
examples: a neutral status text with a small flat dot
an estimated label beside a figure
an unread count beside a menu item

categories.name: Toast and alert
categories.definition: A message about something that happened or a condition that needs attention.

excludes.what: A dialog that blocks the page
A view that replaces missing content

examples: a saved toast with an undo action
an inline warning above a form
a banner about scheduled maintenance

categories.name: Empty and error state
categories.definition: Content that stands in for what is not there: nothing yet, no results, a failure or missing permission.
includes: Dashes in value cells while headers and axes stay

excludes.what: A short message after an action

examples: one line explaining an empty list and one action
a permission view with a request access button
a no results message under a search field

categories.name: Loader and skeleton
categories.definition: An indicator whose only job is to say that something is loading or running, and optionally how far along it is.
includes: Skeleton shapes that mirror the layout

excludes.what: A list of named steps with states
A meter showing a measured quantity
An agent describing its current action in a conversation

examples: pulse shapes shaped like a table
a thin upload progress bar
a small ring beside pending text

categories.name: Overlay: dialog, drawer, popover and menu
categories.definition: A layer above the page that a person opens through a trigger and dismisses: dialogs, drawers, sheets, popovers, tooltips and menus.
includes: Dropdown and context menus of actions

excludes.what: Toasts that appear on their own and block nothing
Mega menus that list global destinations
A select or date field whose options open in a popover

examples: a confirm dialog that says what will be deleted
a sheet sliding in with row details
a definition tooltip beside a metric
a menu of actions from a more button

categories.name: Chart and KPI
categories.definition: Parts that turn measured numbers into marks or figures to read: charts, key figures, gauges and meters.
includes: Line, bar, donut and funnel charts
Key figure tiles with a delta
Heatmaps and relationship charts drawn from data

excludes.what: A number that rolls up as an effect

examples: a figure with label, delta and source
bars ranked by value in one hue
a donut with the key value in the center

categories.name: Table and data grid
categories.definition: Records in rows that share one set of columns with headers.

excludes.what: List rows that share no columns

examples: a table with right aligned figures and hairline rows
a grid with sortable headers and a sticky first column

categories.name: Timeline, stepper and calendar
categories.definition: Items or steps placed in time order or in a fixed sequence: timelines, steppers, wizards and calendars.
includes: Dated event timelines and change logs
Month and week calendars with events
Live step lists of a running process

excludes.what: A how-it-works band on a page
A date field that picks one value

examples: a dated change log with a thin spine
a row of stage dots
a month grid with event chips
a three step signup wizard

categories.name: Map
categories.definition: Things positioned on a map of real places.
includes: Maps with pins linked to a list
Regions shaded by value on a map
examples: a map whose pins filter a list
a world map shaded by region

categories.name: Media and gallery
categories.definition: Images, video or audio that are the content, alone or as a collection to browse.
includes: Two versions of a text side by side

excludes.what: A single item card with a caption

examples: a strip of thumbnails with a play overlay
a draggable divider over an original and an edit
a carousel where the center card is enlarged

categories.name: Commerce
categories.definition: Parts that show goods for sale or move them toward purchase.
includes: Product detail pages and option selectors
Carts, order summaries and checkout steps
examples: a product tile with name and price
an option selector for size and color
a cart with a free shipping line

categories.name: Chat and AI
categories.definition: Parts that live inside a conversation with an AI assistant or agent.
includes: Approval and question steps raised by the agent
examples: a thread with agent replies as plain text
a collapsible line per tool call
an approval card the agent pauses on

categories.name: Motion effect and particles
categories.definition: An effect that animates content which would be complete without it, or a moving decorative backdrop.
includes: Text effects such as typing, scrambling or word cycling
Moving point and line fields behind content
examples: a fade-up on first entry
a seamless logo loop that pauses on hover
a figure that rolls to its value once

categories.name: 3D scene
categories.definition: A scene drawn with depth and a camera, whether it decorates a section or carries content.
includes: Globes and 3D graphs built from real data
examples: a half globe rising from a container edge
a 3D graph built from real data

uses.name: Introduce the product
uses.question: What is this and why should I care?
uses.definition: Tell a first-time visitor what the product is and why it matters.
includes: A headline with one supporting sentence
A first look at the real product

excludes.what: Detail on one capability at a time

examples: the opening headline of a landing page

uses.name: Explain what it does
uses.question: What can it do for me?
uses.definition: Show what the product can do, one capability at a time.
examples: tabs that swap one frame between capabilities

uses.name: Show one number
uses.question: How big or how good is it right now?
uses.definition: Make one current figure readable at a glance.
includes: A key figure with label and delta

excludes.what: How a value changes over time

examples: a monthly revenue figure with a delta

uses.name: Show a trend
uses.question: How is it changing over time?
uses.definition: Show how a value changes over time.
examples: a weekly line chart

uses.name: Compare values
uses.question: Which one is larger or better?
uses.definition: Show which of several items is larger or better.
examples: bars ranked by value

uses.name: Show what it is made of
uses.question: How does the whole split into parts?
uses.definition: Show how a whole splits into parts.
examples: a donut of traffic sources

uses.name: Show where people drop off
uses.question: Where do people leave the process?
uses.definition: Show where people leave a multi-stage process.
examples: a funnel from visit to purchase

uses.name: Show how things relate
uses.question: How are these things connected, or where are they?
uses.definition: Show how things connect to each other or where they are.
examples: pins on a map
a node diagram of integrations

uses.name: Compare plans
uses.question: Which plan fits me?
uses.definition: Help a person choose one plan.
examples: plan cards with a yearly toggle

uses.name: Compare versions
uses.question: What changed between these two?
uses.definition: Show what changed between two versions of the same thing.
examples: a slider over an original and an edit

uses.name: Prove trust
uses.question: Why should I believe this?
uses.definition: Give evidence that the claims on the page are true.
includes: Real customer logos and sourced figures
examples: a quote with a named person and a measured result

uses.name: Answer common questions
uses.question: What do people usually ask?
uses.definition: Answer the questions people usually ask before they decide.
examples: an accordion of questions

uses.name: Ask for the next step
uses.question: What should I do next?
uses.definition: Ask for the next step.
examples: a closing band with one button

uses.name: Capture contact details
uses.question: How do I get in touch or sign up for updates?
uses.definition: Collect contact details to follow up or send updates.
examples: one email field and one button

uses.name: Sign in or sign up
uses.question: How do I get into my account?
uses.definition: Let a person get into an account or create one.
examples: email and password fields with a provider button

uses.name: Guide through steps
uses.question: What are the steps and where am I?
uses.definition: Lead a person through ordered steps and show where they are.
examples: a signup wizard with a step row

uses.name: Show progress
uses.question: Is it working, and how far along is it?
uses.definition: Show that work is running and how far along it is.
examples: an upload progress bar

uses.name: Label a state
uses.question: What is the status of this thing?
uses.definition: Name the status of an item.
examples: a status label on a row

uses.name: Notify the user
uses.question: What just happened, or what needs my attention?
uses.definition: Tell a person what just happened or what needs attention.

excludes.what: A persistent status of an item

examples: a saved toast with undo

uses.name: Confirm an action
uses.question: Am I sure I want to do this?
uses.definition: Make a person confirm an action before it runs.
examples: a delete dialog that asks for the name

uses.name: Explain on demand
uses.question: What does this term or number mean?
uses.definition: Explain a term, figure or control when the person asks.

excludes.what: Showing a whole item in more detail

examples: an info tooltip beside a metric

uses.name: Show details on demand
uses.question: Show me more about this item.
uses.definition: Open more about one item without leaving the screen.
examples: a side sheet with row details

uses.name: Navigate the site
uses.question: Where can I go on this site?
uses.definition: Move between pages of a website.

excludes.what: Moving between areas of an app

examples: a header with page links

uses.name: Navigate the app
uses.question: Where am I in the product and where else can I go?
uses.definition: Move between areas of a product and know where you are.
examples: a grouped sidebar menu

uses.name: Jump anywhere fast
uses.question: Take me straight to that place or command.
uses.definition: Go straight to a place or command by typing.
examples: a command palette

uses.name: Switch views
uses.question: Show me another view or setting of the same thing.
uses.definition: Show another view or setting of the same content.
examples: tabs above a panel

uses.name: Browse many records
uses.question: How do I scan, sort and page through rows?
uses.definition: Scan, sort and page through many records.
examples: a sortable table

uses.name: Filter and search
uses.question: How do I narrow this down?
uses.definition: Narrow a set of items down to the ones that matter.

excludes.what: Going to a place by name

examples: filter chips above a list

uses.name: Enter or pick a value
uses.question: Where do I type or choose something?
uses.definition: Type or pick a value.
examples: a date field

uses.name: Start an action
uses.question: How do I do the thing?
uses.definition: Run the thing the screen is for.
examples: a primary button

uses.name: Handle nothing to show
uses.question: What if there is no data, or something failed?
uses.definition: Say what to do when there is nothing to show or something failed.
examples: an empty list with one action

uses.name: Browse media
uses.question: How do I look through images, video or results?
uses.definition: Look through images, video or results.
examples: a thumbnail strip

uses.name: Sell a product
uses.question: How do I see a product and buy it?
uses.definition: Show a product and let a person buy it.
examples: a product detail page

uses.name: Ask the assistant
uses.question: How do I talk to the AI and read its answer?
uses.definition: Talk to an AI assistant and read its answer.
examples: a chat thread with a composer

uses.name: Set the mood
uses.question: How do I give the page atmosphere without clutter?
uses.definition: Give a page atmosphere without adding information.
examples: a slow moving point field

uses.name: Make a phrase land
uses.question: How do I draw attention to a line of text?
uses.definition: Make one line of text land.
examples: a pull quote

uses.name: Organize the page
uses.question: How is the page laid out and its content grouped?
uses.definition: Lay out the page and group its content.
examples: wider spacing between unrelated groups

uses.name: Read long text
uses.question: How do I read an article or a policy comfortably?
uses.definition: Read an article or a policy comfortably.
examples: a reading column

uses.name: Set the visual foundation
uses.question: Which tokens, type, icons and marks does everything share?
uses.definition: Choose the tokens, type, icons and marks everything shares.
examples: a token theme with light and dark sets

uses.name: Show when things happen
uses.question: What happened or is scheduled, and in what order?
uses.definition: Show what happened or is scheduled, in order.

excludes.what: How a value changes over time

examples: a change log

surfaces.name: Marketing landing page
surfaces.definition: A public page that introduces a product or offer to a visitor and asks for one action.

excludes.what: Pages that sell goods with a cart

examples: a product home page
a launch page for one feature

surfaces.name: Dashboard and analytics
surfaces.definition: A screen that monitors figures and trends for a person who returns to it often.

excludes.what: Screens for doing tasks on records

examples: a weekly metrics overview

surfaces.name: Product app and tools
surfaces.definition: A signed-in product screen where a person creates, edits or manages things.
examples: a project list with row actions
a settings page

surfaces.name: Store and product pages
surfaces.definition: Pages that show goods for sale and take an order.
examples: a product detail page with options

surfaces.name: Articles, documents and papers
surfaces.definition: Pages made to be read: articles, documents, reports and policies.

excludes.what: Pages that ask for one action

examples: a long article
a printed report sheet

surfaces.name: Sign in and onboarding
surfaces.definition: Screens that get a person into an account and through their first steps.
examples: a sign in page
a three step setup wizard

surfaces.name: AI chat and agent
surfaces.definition: Screens where a person works with an AI assistant or agent in a conversation.
includes: Agent runs with tool calls and approvals
examples: an agent thread with tool calls

axes.name: Density
axes.definition: How much fits in one view: spacing between and inside groups, control height and body line height.

anchors.0: Spacious: wide gaps between sections and inside cards, tall controls, relaxed line height.
anchors.1: Compact: tight gaps, 32px controls on wide screens, body line height near 1.4; data screens only.
anchors.0.5: Regular: the shipped 4px grid, 36px controls, body line height 1.5.

axes.rationale: The first thing a builder decides between a marketing page and a data screen. --control-touch is not driven, so touch targets stay 44px (RSP-06).

axes.name: Contrast
axes.definition: How far text, muted text and surfaces step apart in lightness.

anchors.0: Washed out: muted text under 4.5:1 and surfaces barely step. Never allowed, see the contrast floor.
anchors.1: Maximum: muted text close to body text, surfaces and sunken areas clearly stepped.
anchors.0.5: Standard: muted text well above 4.5:1, surfaces step by a small tone.

axes.rationale: Separation by tone is the alternative to borders and shadows, and its floor is an accessibility line, not a taste.

axes.name: Roundness
axes.definition: Corner radius of containers and controls, from one base value scaled by element size.

anchors.0: Square corners on every container and control.
anchors.1: Pillow: about 20px or more on cards; full pills only on small controls.
anchors.0.5: Soft: about 8 to 10px on cards, smaller on controls.

axes.rationale: Radius is the most visible single value of a brand tone. --r-pill is not driven, pills stay pills.

axes.name: Type expression
axes.definition: How loud the type is: the heading face and how far display sizes rise above body text.

anchors.0: Quiet: one neutral face, display about 1.6 times body, small weight steps.
anchors.1: Poster: an expressive display face, display four times body or more, tight leading on headlines.
anchors.0.5: Branded: a chosen face for headings, display about 2.5 times body.

axes.rationale: Body and small sizes (--t-body, --t-sm, --t-xs, --t-micro) are not driven: they are readability floors (KO-11), not tone.

axes.name: Color restraint
axes.definition: How few hues the interface uses outside real outcomes; higher means more restraint.

anchors.0: Rainbow: every box, badge and series in its own hue. Never allowed, see the restraint floor.
anchors.1: Achromatic: neutral surfaces and one brand slot, semantic colors only for real outcomes.
anchors.0.5: Two hues: the brand hue plus one secondary highlight, semantic colors for outcomes.

axes.rationale: Named as restraint, not saturation, because the slop tell is the count of hues, not their strength.

axes.name: Elevation
axes.definition: How much surfaces rise above the page: shadow depth, raised surface tone and the scrim behind overlays.

anchors.0: Flat: surfaces separated by tone and borders only, no shadow.
anchors.1: Layered: clear shadows on every raised surface and a dense scrim behind overlays.
anchors.0.5: Raised: a small shadow on cards and a larger one on floating layers.

axes.rationale: Depth is how a surface claims attention; it is coupled to radius, borders and hue below.

axes.name: Motion
axes.definition: How much and how long things move: durations, entrance offset and scale, stagger and crossfade blur.

anchors.0: Still: state changes are instant, only opacity and color fade.
anchors.1: Expressive: entrance and scroll-linked motion on landing bands, overlays near 400ms.
anchors.0.5: Standard: UI feedback under 300ms with ease-out, no entrance animation on blocks.

axes.rationale: Easing curves are not driven: their shapes are fixed by the motion rules, only amount and length move. prefers-reduced-motion still overrides every value.

axes.name: Stroke
axes.definition: How visible lines are: border opacity and weight on containers and fields, and the icon stroke.

anchors.0: None: no borders, surfaces separated by tone steps; icons at 1.5 units.
anchors.1: Heavy: clearly visible borders and icons at 2 units.
anchors.0.5: Light: one pixel borders at low opacity on containers and fields.

axes.rationale: Replaces the suggested ornament axis. Ornament has no token in tokens.css, and Taster treats decoration (blobs, glows, gradient text) as a rule to pass, not a dial to turn: a dial for it would make slop a setting. Line weight is the real, token-backed part of a decorative tone.

constraints.principle: Muted and small text keep at least 4.5:1 against every surface, so contrast never drops to the washed-out end.
Hue is reserved for the brand and for real outcomes; below this floor every box, badge and series gets its own tint.
The more a screen holds, the quieter its type: a compact data screen cannot carry poster headlines.
The more a screen holds, the less of it moves: dense screens animate feedback, not entrances.
A surface is separated by a border or by a shadow; heavy borders plus deep shadows double every edge and turn nesting into boxes in boxes.
Large radius and deep soft shadow together are the default generated card; one of the two carries the softness.
Radius and depth describe one material: shadows may not run more than two steps ahead of the corner radius.
Radius and depth describe one material: the corner radius may not run more than two steps ahead of the shadows.
Deep shadows only on a restrained palette, because depth plus free hue is how colored glows and neon halos appear.
Type and color do not both shout: the louder the type, the fewer hues around it.

iconography.summary: Where an icon belongs and what it must look like. Decide the slot first, then whether the slot needs an icon at all, then draw it from the one set. Pattern: icon-placement.

set.style: One family. Outline only or filled only, never both on one page. Filled is allowed only as the selected state of an outline icon.
set.stroke: One stroke width for the whole set, 1.5 to 2 units on the 24 grid, round caps and joins.
set.color: currentColor. The parent sets the color with a text token; no per-icon hue.
set.alignment: Center the icon on the first line of its label, not on the whole text block. 16px beside 14 to 16px text, 20px beside 18 to 20px text.
set.accessibility: Decorative icons get aria-hidden. An icon-only control gets an accessible name on the control.

slots.name: Control icon
slots.covers: Buttons, toolbar actions, navigation items, close, menu, search, disclosure chevrons, external link, download.
slots.test: Does the icon trigger, open, close or move something?
slots.keep_when: The icon is the control itself (icon-only button), or it is a convention people scan for (search, close, menu, back, more, external link).
slots.instead: A text label. A primary action with a clear verb needs no leading icon.
slots.accessibility: Icon-only control: aria-label on the button, aria-hidden on the svg, a 44px hit area.

slots.name: Explanatory icon
slots.covers: Feature cards, benefit lists, category entries, file types, step lists.
slots.test: Would a reader lose information if the icon were removed?
slots.keep_when: The icon carries meaning the words do not: a file type, an integration, a category that repeats elsewhere as a filter or navigation key. It is chosen for that item, not to fill a slot.
slots.instead: Nothing. Or a number with its unit, a short label, a real screenshot or product crop, or a list with plain bullets.
slots.accessibility: aria-hidden, because the text beside it says the same thing.

slots.name: Identity mark
slots.covers: The product logo, partner and integration logos, payment and platform marks, people in avatars.
slots.test: Does the mark stand for a specific brand, product or person?
slots.keep_when: Always, but only as the original asset: the supplied vector, the owner's official file, or the person's photo.
slots.instead: A marked placeholder and a request for the file. Initials for a person without a photo. Never a redrawn lookalike or a generic glyph standing in for a brand.
slots.accessibility: Alt text with the brand or person name, or empty alt when the name is printed beside it.

slots.name: Data marker
slots.covers: Trend arrows, legend swatches, check and cross marks in comparison tables, chart markers. Status (live, failed, paused) is written as a word, not a colored dot.
slots.test: Does the mark encode a value or a state that is also written next to it?
slots.keep_when: It sits beside the number or word it encodes and uses shape as well as color, so it reads in grayscale.
slots.instead: The word or the number alone. A status label instead of a colored dot. A table cell with "Included" or a dash reads faster than a column of green discs.
slots.accessibility: The text carries the meaning; the marker is aria-hidden. Color is never the only signal.

slots.name: No icon
slots.covers: Headlines and section headings, hero copy, section kickers, paragraphs, FAQ questions, footer columns, every item of a long list.
slots.test: Is the icon only there because the slot looked empty?
slots.keep_when: Never. These slots are carried by type, space and real content.
slots.instead: Size, weight and space for hierarchy. A real image or number when the section needs a visual.
slots.accessibility: Nothing to label, because nothing is drawn.
